title: A Cover for the Deadline
premise: Astrid Voss, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Bureau—an embassy that exists on no map—has spent a decade erasing himself from every record, including his own past. When a burner phone he never purchased rings with the voice of his presumed-dead mentor, Elias Brandt, Astrid is pulled into a conspiracy to expose the Bureau at the upcoming Helsinki summit. As he hunts the caller, he uncovers that his erased memories were not lost but surgically taken, and that the voice belongs to a man who helped take them. In the end, Astrid chooses to trade his last protected secret—the location of the Bureau's archive of stolen identities—to a summit journalist, burning the Bureau down and reclaiming his name, at the cost of any place left to belong.
about_author: Isandro Voss is the pseudonym of a former diplomatic courier who spent eleven years moving sealed pouches across borders that officially didn't exist. He writes thrillers from a different country every year, and refuses to confirm which ones.

chapters.title: The Phone That Wasn't Issued
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Between routine deniable errands in Vienna, Astrid finds a burner phone in his own coat pocket—unregistered, untraceable, impossible. When it rings, the voice is Elias Brandt, his mentor dead for six years. The beat is cold unease: the invisible man has been found, and he didn't even feel the touch.

chapters.title: Deniable Assets
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He reports nothing and instead audits his own Bureau file, finding a gap: three missing weeks in 2014 that even he can't account for. His handler, Mireille, notices his digging. Emotional beat: the first crack of distrust—Astrid realizes he's investigating himself as much as the caller.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with an intercut of the caller's. The phone rings again; Brandt's voice recites details of Astrid's erased childhood—a harbor town, a sister—things no file contains. Astrid verifies the voiceprint against old intercepts: it's genuinely Elias. Beat: grief resurfacing under tradecraft, memory as a wound reopened.

chapters.title: The Meridian Ledger
chapters.summary: Sister-chapter from the caller's POV, unnamed. We learn someone is cataloguing the Bureau's stolen identities for exposure before the Helsinki summit, and that Astrid is both target and key. Beat: dread reframed—the reader sees Astrid is a weapon being aimed, not a hunter.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A meet arranged through dead drop goes wrong; Mireille's cleaners arrive instead of the caller. Astrid escapes using a route from his missing three weeks—muscle memory he shouldn't have. Beat: vertigo and adrenaline; his body remembers what his mind was made to forget.

chapters.title: The Harbor Town
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He goes off-grid to the harbor town from the calls and finds a woman who recognizes him: his sister Lene, alive, who says he chose to be erased. Beat: belonging offered and refused—Astrid can't tell if he's reclaiming a past or being handed a fabricated one.

chapters.title: What Mireille Kept
chapters.summary: Mireille's POV. She reveals to the reader (and later Astrid) that she authorized his memory wipe to protect him from a Bureau purge, and that Brandt helped—then turned against them. Beat: betrayal and loyalty tangled; the handler who lied to save him now must decide whether to save him again.

chapters.title: Helsinki, Two Days Out
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The caller summons him: Elias is alive, complicit in the wipe, and offers the truth in exchange for the archive's location. Astrid learns the Bureau plans to eliminate him as a loose end before the summit. Beat: cornered clarity—he stops running and starts choosing.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax. In the summit's shadow, Astrid meets Elias, confronts the man who unmade him, and instead of giving the archive to either Elias or the Bureau, hands its location to an investigative journalist mid-broadcast. Elias dies in the ensuing Bureau sweep; Mireille lets Astrid walk. Beat: rage transmuted into sacrifice.

chapters.title: A Name, Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, resolution. The Bureau unravels publicly; identities are returned. Astrid visits Lene, gives her his true name, and disappears—not erased this time, but self-chosen. Final beat: bittersweet belonging—he can never fully return, but for the first time, he exists on his own terms.
